title: Levofloxacin
dek: The other TB fluoroquinolone: 6Lfx TPT for FQ-S MDR contacts, Hr-TB 6REZ-Lfx, BDLLfxC, many 9-month recipes. Same QRDR as moxi; different trials and often less QTc than moxi.
story: Levofloxacin (usual 750–1000 mg daily in adults, weight-banded in children) is the FQ WHO writes into 6-month levofloxacin TPT for contacts of FQ-susceptible MDR/RR-TB, into Hr-TB (6REZ-Lfx), into BDLLfxC, and into several 9-month orals. Moxifloxacin occupies BPaLM and HPMZ. Pick the FQ the regimen was studied with unless your NTP explicitly swaps.
QRDR cross-resistance is the default prior. A D94G source makes 6Lfx TPT misbuilt. A D94G patient makes BDLLfxC prune Lfx (continue BDLC).
Often slightly friendlier on QTc than moxi, still a FQ for tendons, CNS, and empiric-pneumonia abuse. Renal clearance: adjust when GFR falls (unlike moxi’s more hepatic mix).
deep: 6Lfx TPT is daily LFX for 6 months after disease exclusion — not a week of cough medicine.
Children tolerate LFX in DR-TB with attention to musculoskeletal AEs.
Do not combine MXF and LFX as two FQs. They are one mechanism.

visual.caption: Levofloxacin’s WHO jobs. All of them assume a live QRDR. None of them is BPaLM’s M (that is moxi).
